# -*- mode: ruby -*-
# vi: set ft=ruby :

# First we define two (large multiline) strings, $script and $msg, to be
# used later

$script = <<-'SCRIPT'
set -xe
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
apt-get -qq update
# apt-get -qq upgrade -y
apt-get -qq install -y apt-transport-https ca-certificates curl \
               software-properties-common \
               nasm zip strace binutils build-essential \
               gdb gdb-doc gdbserver \
               manpages-posix-dev manpages-posix \
               vim emacs-nox nano bash-completion git file \
               python3-dev python3-pip python3-ropgadget \
               curl wget clang xz-utils \
               sl lolcat socat cowsay cowsay-off filters bsdgames \
               afl++ afl++-doc checksec \
               qemu-user-static gdb-multiarch
pip3 install -U ROPgadget 'capstone>=5.0,<6.0'

# If we want GDB to be able to attach to an other process we
# need to switch off some kernel hardening.
# We do this by changing the ptrace scope from one to zero
sed -i 's/kernel.yama.ptrace_scope = 1/kernel.yama.ptrace_scope = 0/' /etc/sysctl.d/10-ptrace.conf

# We then need to restart the relevant service
sysctl -p /etc/sysctl.d/10-ptrace.conf

# Disable Canonical phone-home motd
sed -i 's/ENABLED=1/ENABLED=0/' /etc/default/motd-news

# Install RV32
RV32_DIR=/opt/riscv32
mkdir -p "$RV32_DIR"
RV32_URL="https://github.com/riscv-collab/riscv-gnu-toolchain/releases/download/2026.06.06/riscv32-glibc-ubuntu-22.04-gcc.tar.xz"
curl -fL --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 "$RV32_URL" -o /tmp/rv32-toolchain.tar.xz
tar -xJf /tmp/rv32-toolchain.tar.xz -C "$RV32_DIR"
rm -f /tmp/rv32-toolchain.tar.xz

# Figure out where inside /opt/riscv32 the toolchain ended up, and set up environment variables accordingly.
RV32_GCC=$(find "$RV32_DIR" -type f -name 'riscv32-*-gcc' | head -1)
if [ -z "$RV32_GCC" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: rv32 gcc not found after extracting the toolchain." >&2
  exit 1
fi
RV32_BIN=$(dirname "$RV32_GCC")
RV32_SYSROOT=$("$RV32_GCC" -print-sysroot)

# Put the toolchain on PATH so binariess can be invoked as rv32-gcc, rv32-objdump, etc. in the current shell.
export PATH="$RV32_BIN:$PATH"

# Make DYNAMICALLY-linked rv32 binaries runnable via binfmt (./prog) 
sed -i '/^QEMU_LD_PREFIX=/d' /etc/environment
echo "QEMU_LD_PREFIX=$RV32_SYSROOT" >> /etc/environment
echo "export QEMU_LD_PREFIX=$RV32_SYSROOT" >> /etc/profile.d/riscv32.sh
export QEMU_LD_PREFIX="$RV32_SYSROOT"

# Create short, intuitive aliases: rv32-gcc, rv32-objdump, rv32-as, rv32-ld,
# rv32-objcopy, rv32-readelf, ... instead of riscv32-unknown-linux-gnu-*.
echo Creating rv32-* command aliases
RV32_PREFIX=$(basename "$RV32_GCC")
RV32_PREFIX=${RV32_PREFIX%gcc}
for f in "$RV32_BIN/${RV32_PREFIX}"*; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || continue
  tool=$(basename "$f")
  tool=${tool#"$RV32_PREFIX"}
  ln -sf "$f" "/usr/local/bin/rv32-$tool"
done

# compile and install runshellcode tool, a PCS specific program for running shellcode
echo Installing runshellcode program
cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/runshellcode.c
#include <sys/types.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
  char *stack_space[0x1000];
  int fd;
  struct stat sbuf;
  void (*shellcode)(void);
  int i, z, c, bufsize, numb;
  unsigned char *p;
  if (argc < 2) {
    fprintf(stderr, "Usage: %s (<filename>|-)\n", argv[0]);
    return EXIT_FAILURE;
  }

  if (strcmp(argv[1], "-") == 0) {
    bufsize = 4096;
    p = malloc(bufsize);
    z = 0;
    numb = 0;
    while ((c = getchar()) != EOF) {
      if (numb == bufsize) {
        bufsize += 4096;
        p = realloc(p, bufsize);
      }
      p[numb++] = c;
      if (c == '\0') z++;
    }

    if ((shellcode = mmap(NULL, numb, PROT_READ | PROT_EXEC | PROT_WRITE,
                          MAP_ANONYMOUS | MAP_PRIVATE, -1, 0)) == MAP_FAILED) {
      perror("mmap() failed");
      return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    memcpy(shellcode, p, numb);
    free(p);
  } else {
    if ((fd = open(argv[1], O_RDONLY)) < 0) {
      perror("open() failed");
      return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    if (fstat(fd, &sbuf)) {
      perror("fstat() failed");
      return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    if ((shellcode = mmap(NULL, sbuf.st_size, PROT_READ | PROT_EXEC | PROT_WRITE,
                          MAP_PRIVATE, fd, 0)) == MAP_FAILED) {
      perror("mmap() failed");
      return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    close(fd);
    for (i = 0, z = 0, p = (void *)shellcode; i < sbuf.st_size; i++) {
      if (p[i] == '\0') z++;
    }
    numb = sbuf.st_size;
  }

  argc--;
  for (i = 0; i < argc; i++) {
    argv[i] = argv[i + 1];
  }

  fprintf(stderr, "Read %d bytes of shell code. Here goes.\n", numb);
  if (z > 0) fprintf(stderr, "Shellcode contains %d zero bytes.\n", z);
  fprintf(stderr, "~~~ Running shellcode ~~~\n");

  shellcode();

  /* should not be reached */
  return EXIT_FAILURE;
}
EOF
cd /tmp
gcc -z execstack -fno-stack-protector runshellcode.c -o /usr/bin/runshellcode

# rv32 build
"$RV32_GCC" -static -z execstack -fno-stack-protector \
    runshellcode.c -o /usr/bin/runshellcode-riscv


# Create rv32gdb at /usr/local/bin/rv32gdb
cat <<'RVGDB' > /usr/local/bin/rv32gdb
#!/bin/sh
set -e
if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
  echo "usage: rv32gdb <binary> [args...]" >&2
  exit 1
fi
PORT="${RV32GDB_PORT:-1234}"
BIN="$1"; shift



# QEMU_LD_PREFIX is set in /etc/environment, so dynamic binaries resolve too.
qemu-riscv32-static -g "$PORT" "$BIN" "$@" &
QPID=$!
trap 'kill "$QPID" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
gdb-multiarch -q "$BIN" \
  -ex "set architecture riscv:rv32" \
  -ex "set sysroot $RV32_SYSROOT" \
  -ex "target remote :$PORT"
RVGDB
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/rv32gdb

SCRIPT

$msg = <<~MSG
------------------------------------------------------
The PCS VM is ready

Get ssh access with the command
    vagrant ssh

The files in the current directory can be found
in the /vagrant directory

RISC-V 32-bit toolchain is available as rv32-gcc, rv32-as, etc.
Use rv32gdb <binary> to debug rv32 binaries with gdb-multiarch.
------------------------------------------------------
MSG

Vagrant.configure(2) do |config|
  config.vm.define "Proactive Computer Security F2026"

  # Every Vagrant virtual environment requires a box to build off
  # of. We build of Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish)
  config.vm.box = "ubuntu/jammy64"

  config.vm.hostname = "pcs-f2026"
  # config.vm.network "forwarded_port", guest: 22, host: 2222,
  #                    host_ip: "127.0.0.1", id: 'ssh'

  # This ought to be default, but some boxes leave it out, so we ask
  # for it explicitly
  config.vm.synced_folder ".", "/vagrant"

  # provider for virtualbox on intel
  config.vm.provider "virtualbox" do |vb|
    vb.memory = "4096"
    vb.cpus = 2

    # Fix console
    # https://bugs.launchpad.net/cloud-images/+bug/1829625
    vb.customize ["modifyvm", :id, "--uart1", "0x3F8", "4"]
    vb.customize ["modifyvm", :id, "--uartmode1", "file", File::NULL]

    # Display the VirtualBox GUI when booting the machine
    # vb.gui = true
   end

  # provider for libvirt, e.g. virt-manager
  config.vm.provider "libvirt" do |lv, override|
    lv.default_prefix = ""
    lv.random_hostname = false

    lv.memory = 4096
    lv.cpus = 2

    # we might be able to use this image as default, for both providers
    override.vm.box = "alvistack/ubuntu-22.04"
  end

  # Create a private network, which allows host-only access to the
  # machine using a specific IP.
  #config.vm.network "private_network", ip: "192.168.33.42"

  # Share an additional folder to the guest VM.
  # The first argument is the path on the host to the actual folder.
  # The second argument is the path on the guest to mount the folder.
  #config.vm.synced_folder "./src", "/pcs"

  # Define the script: A shell script that runs after first
  # setup of your box (= provisioning). Here using the inline script defined in
  # the top of the file.

  # Install some useful tools, compile runshellcode.c, and set up rv32 toolchain
  config.vm.provision :shell, name: "Install PCS Tools", inline: $script

  # Add minimal .gdbinit and disable Canonical ads
  config.vm.provision :shell, name: "Add minimal .gdbinit for the normal user",
                      privileged: false, inline: <<-'SHELL'
set -xe
cat <<'EOF' > .gdbinit
# Settings
set disassembly-flavor intel
set disable-randomization off
set pagination off
set follow-fork-mode child

# History
set history filename ~/.gdbhistory
set history save
set history expansion

# Output format
#set output-radix 0x10

# Connect to a local qemu-riscv32 gdb stub. Usage: rvconnect [port] (default 1234)
define rvconnect
  set architecture riscv:rv32
  if $argc == 0
    target remote :1234
  else
    target remote :$arg0
  end
end
document rvconnect
Connect gdb to a local qemu-riscv32 stub. Usage: rvconnect [port] (default 1234)
end

EOF
touch $HOME/.hushlogin
SHELL


  config.vm.post_up_message = $msg

end
